canonical_title: SAP replaces expensive AI models with cheaper alternatives; targets over EUR 2 billion efficiency gains
treatment: Repeat only for concrete new policy, realized outcomes or independently verified implementation details.
known_facts: Reuters published 2026-10-28 14:08 UTC (23:08 JST), citing SAP CFO Dominik Asam.
SAP has replaced some costly AI models in its products including its internal consulting assistant with cheaper alternatives where quality remains sufficient.
SAP expects more than EUR 2 billion of efficiency gains over two years; this is a company forecast, not realized savings.
SAP uses more than 70 AI models and increasingly selects the lowest-cost model meeting task requirements; overall AI spending is still expected to rise.
SAP charges customers for completed tasks rather than underlying model compute; model-origin restrictions and demand for local models affect routing.
reinclude_only_if: Official quantified realized savings or revised targets
Named model routing policy, benchmarks, task-quality results or pricing changes
Material changes to model provider list, residency restrictions or production rollout
